tasks.short: Read each application against the job order and decide who goes through to the hiring manager.

steps.what: Check must-haves: right to work, licence, certificate, shift availability, travel distance
Read CV and letter for employers, dates, certificates, gaps and languages

loop.input: CV and letter text or image from Recruitee, plus the job order must-haves
loop.output: structured profile: employers with dates, certificates, licences, languages, distance to site; missing must-haves listed; no score
loop.check: dates parse and do not overlap impossibly; each field quotes the CV span it came from; age, photo, nationality and health are never extracted
loop.stop: one pass plus one retry; a CV that cannot be read goes to the recruiter marked read by hand
loop.why_not_simpler: CVs are free text and photos; Recruitee's parsed fields miss certificates and shift experience

steps.what: Decide screen in, screen out, or ask the manager
Move the stage in Recruitee and write the reason
Chase the hiring manager when the job order is vague

tasks.design: A job-order intake form with must-haves as fields, so a vacancy cannot open without them. Recruitee knock-out questions sort applications into queues (all must-haves, one missing, right to work missing); a bounded extraction loop turns each CV into a profile card that lists facts and missing items, never a score. The recruiter works the queue in Recruitee and decides; every decision and its reason is logged and kept six months.
tasks.previous_blocker: Must-haves lived in the manager's head and in mail threads, CVs arrive as PDFs and photos, and a screening tool meant a score that the works council and the AP would not accept.
tasks.enabler_now: Recruitee's API and questionnaires, models that read CVs well enough when every field quotes its source, and a clear legal line: facts and queues are allowed, automated rejection is not.
tasks.still_hard: Vague job orders, candidates who apply to every vacancy, and proving to the works council that the loop extracts nothing it should not.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a candidate with a thin CV but the right shift history will stay, and knowing which team lead will give them a chance.

ambition.what: Every application gets a decision within one working day, including weekend applications for shift roles.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter opens the week with a sorted queue instead of a pile, and gains the right to refuse a vacancy without complete must-haves.

reach.learn: Which must-haves predict 90-day retention per site, read from the funnel dashboard

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 builds a profile from the application and a match score; no accuracy figure
CV screening with AI almost always needs prior works council consent; nullity within one month
No rejection based solely on a score; the review must be real
Filtering applications is high-risk under Annex III from 2 December 2027
26% of US hiring leaders fear they no longer see some candidates because of AI screening
Liability stays with the employer; match scores from data beyond the application are under attack

assumptions: Most hires are warehouse and transport roles with a short list of hard must-haves
Recruitee questionnaires can hold knock-out questions per job profile
unknowns: Applications per week per site and the share that fails a must-have
Minutes per application today
Whether the works council accepts a queue-and-card tool without a score
research_questions: Of last year's applications, what share failed a hard must-have a questionnaire would have caught?
How many candidates waited more than five working days for a first decision?
How often does the recruiter overrule a must-have, and did those hires stay?

tasks.short: Tell candidates what the job pays, the shifts, conditions and prospects, by mail, phone and at offer.

steps.what: Look up pay scale, shift pattern, allowances and start dates per vacancy
Write and send the vacancy information mail
Answer candidate questions by mail or phone

loop.input: a candidate's mail question plus the vacancy fact sheet
loop.output: a draft reply with the fact sheet line it rests on
loop.check: every fact in the draft maps to a fact sheet field; questions outside the sheet get no draft, only a flag
loop.stop: one draft; the recruiter edits and sends from their own mailbox; phone questions are out of scope
loop.why_not_simpler: questions are free text and mix pay, shifts and travel in one mail

steps.what: Explain the offer and conditions in a call

tasks.design: A vacancy fact sheet generated from AFAS (scale, allowances) and the job order (shifts, site, start dates), shown on the Recruitee job page and merged into every candidate mail. A bounded loop drafts replies to mail questions from the sheet; the recruiter sends. Phone and offer calls stay.
tasks.previous_blocker: Pay and shift facts sat in the CAO, AFAS and the manager's head; every answer was looked up again.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS scale tables over the connector, Recruitee job pages with structured fields, and the Article 50 line that recruiter-reviewed mail needs no AI label.
tasks.still_hard: CAO changes and site allowances must be kept current; candidates on shifts call rather than mail.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what the candidate is really asking (can I pick up my children at 15:00) and answering that.

ambition.what: Weekend and night applicants get the fact sheet and a reply within an hour, where today they wait for Monday.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter answers the question behind the question and stops looking up pay scales; they own the fact sheet per job profile.

reach.task: Explain contract and conditions at signing
reach.learn: Contract clauses and CAO allowances per site

evidence.claim: A candidate mail a recruiter has substantively reviewed needs no AI label; a chatbot must say it is AI at the first turn
Job descriptions are the third most common AI use among US hiring leaders (57%)
Recruitee job pages hold structured vacancy fields

assumptions: Pay scale per job profile is in AFAS and allowances per site are written down
unknowns: Share of candidate questions that arrive by phone versus mail
How often an answer today is wrong or inconsistent between the two recruiters
research_questions: Which ten questions do candidates ask most, and are they on the job page?
How many offer declines cite pay or shift surprises?

tasks.short: Pick a shortlist, write it up for the manager, chase a decision, record it and hand over for the offer.

steps.what: Compare screened-in candidates and pick a shortlist
Write candidate summaries for the hiring manager
Send the shortlist and chase the manager for a response
Discuss the pick with the manager and agree who to interview or hire
Record the decision in Recruitee and hand over to HR admin for the offer

tasks.design: The candidate card is a template filled from Recruitee fields and the profile card, with two lines the recruiter types. It goes to the manager in Teams with a one-tap invite, no or talk form, a reminder after two working days and an escalation after five. The hire stage in Recruitee creates the pre-boarding record in AFAS.
tasks.previous_blocker: Summaries were written from scratch in Word and sent by mail; managers on shifts answered late and the recruiter chased by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Recruitee and AFAS connectors, Teams forms over Graph, and managers who carry a phone on the floor.
tasks.still_hard: Managers who want the full CV anyway, and the line between a factual card and an evaluation that counts as high-risk.
tasks.human_edge: Arguing for the candidate the manager would have skipped, and reading the manager's hesitation.

ambition.what: Managers answer a shortlist within one working day instead of at the next weekly call.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter spends the saved hours in the manager conversation and gains a standing escalation when a shortlist waits more than five days.

reach.learn: AFAS pre-boarding fields and the contract template per CAO

evidence.claim: Uniper's agent flagged overdue recruiter and manager tasks; time to contract fell 27 days (vendor figures, no baseline)
Workday's agent drafts outreach and feedback but a recruiter approves before anything is sent
AI summaries become the record managers read instead of the interview; summaries drop context
Evaluating candidates is high-risk under Annex III from 2 December 2027

assumptions: Managers accept a one-tap Teams form
The works council treats a factual card without ranking as different from a screening score
unknowns: Days a shortlist waits for a manager today
Whether Recruitee's hire stage can trigger AFAS pre-boarding through the connector
research_questions: How many days do shortlists wait per site and manager?
Did candidates who waited longer decline more offers?

tasks.short: Book and run forklift tests, safety inductions, driver medicals and assessments for candidates.

steps.what: Work out which tests and checks the job profile needs
Find a slot with the candidate, the trainer or provider and a forklift
Run the test or induction with the candidate
Record the result and file the certificate or fitness statement
Chase no-shows and rebook

tasks.design: A checklist per job profile decides the tests; a booking link over the trainer's or provider's Outlook calendar lets the candidate pick a slot, with confirmation, a reminder 24 hours before and an automatic rebook offer after a no-show. A phone form records pass or fail into Recruitee and, after hire, into Studytube. The test itself stays with the trainer and recruiter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Three calendars (candidate, trainer, forklift) were matched by phone; results were mailed and retyped.
tasks.enabler_now: Graph calendar access and the Recruitee and Studytube APIs; the booking page is a day of work.
tasks.still_hard: Medical results are pass or fail only and must not be stored further; external assessment providers have their own portals.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing on the forklift whether someone is safe, not just whether they pass.

ambition.what: Flex workers get the same induction booking and certificate check before day one as employees.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter stops dialling three parties per test and gains the right to set the test checklist per job profile with L&D.

reach.learn: Studytube course set-up and certificate expiry rules

evidence.claim: Scheduling is the second most common AI use among US hiring leaders (59%)
Pre-employment medicals are limited to job demands and the employer learns fitness only (Wet op de medische keuringen)
Health data is special-category data under GDPR and needs a legal basis and minimal storage

assumptions: Warehouse trainers keep their Outlook calendar current
Driver medicals are booked with an external provider by mail
unknowns: Tests per month per site
No-show rate today
research_questions: How many test bookings were rescheduled at least once last year?
Which tests are required per job profile today, in writing?

tasks.short: Tell candidates where they stand: received, invited, on hold or rejected, by mail or phone.

steps.what: Check which candidates are waiting for news
Send acknowledgements, invitations and holding messages
Send rejections after screening
Call or write personally to candidates rejected after interview or offer
Answer any-news calls and mails

tasks.design: Recruitee stage changes trigger templated messages; a daily rule finds candidates with no movement for seven days and sends a holding message or nudges the recruiter. Screening rejections go out in a reviewed batch with a reason category. Rejections after an interview stay a call.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates existed but were sent by hand; nobody saw who had been silent for two weeks.
tasks.enabler_now: Recruitee's API exposes stage events; the seven-day rule is a few lines of code.
tasks.still_hard: Candidates who come through agencies or boards without a Recruitee record; tone in Dutch and English for shift workers.
tasks.human_edge: A rejection call after an interview that leaves the candidate willing to apply again.

ambition.what: No candidate is silent for more than seven days, including those on hold.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter sends nothing routine and reviews one rejection batch a day; they own the templates and the silence rule.

evidence.claim: Uniper's agent coordinated candidate mails and found 27 candidates on a shortlist for more than 14 days
Templated status mail with no generated text needs no AI label
Candidate trust and drop-off was a named issue for 11% of surveyed US leaders

assumptions: Recruitee templates can carry the vacancy fact sheet fields
unknowns: Candidates per month who withdraw without a message
Whether candidates prefer SMS or WhatsApp over mail
research_questions: How many candidates were silent for more than seven days last quarter, and how many of them withdrew?

tasks.short: Find candidates: job boards, the own talent pool, LinkedIn, referrals, fairs, schools and agencies.

steps.what: Post the vacancy on job boards and social media
Search the talent pool and past applicants
Search LinkedIn and write outreach messages

loop.input: the vacancy fact sheet and the profile text the recruiter pastes in
loop.output: a short outreach message in the recruiter's name
loop.check: no claim outside the fact sheet; no reference to age, origin or health; under 120 words
loop.stop: one draft per candidate; the recruiter edits and sends from their own account; no automated sending
loop.why_not_simpler: a template reads as spam; the message must say why this person

steps.what: Run the referral programme: tips, tracking, bonus at day 90
Job fairs, open days and school visits

tasks.design: Recruitee multiposting for boards; a talent-pool query on profile card fields with a retention and consent check; a referral form in Teams that tags the candidate in Recruitee and triggers the bonus to payroll at day 90; a bounded loop drafts outreach the recruiter sends in their own name. Fairs and schools stay.
tasks.previous_blocker: The talent pool was never searchable by certificate or shift; referrals ran in Excel and bonuses were forgotten.
tasks.enabler_now: Profile cards from task 1 make the pool searchable; Graph forms and AFAS connectors make the referral loop small.
tasks.still_hard: Retention rules limit the pool to a year with consent; LinkedIn terms forbid scraping, so the search stays a person's work.
tasks.human_edge: Standing at the Venlo school fair and spotting who will like warehouse work.

ambition.what: Re-contact every past silver-medal candidate within a day of a similar vacancy opening.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter sources at fairs and in schools instead of posting and tracking; they own the channel mix per job profile.

reach.learn: BBL apprenticeship routes and the school calendar

evidence.claim: Workday's agent surfaces qualified applicants and drafts outreach; the recruiter approves each send
An outbound sourcing agent must say it is AI and for whom; a recruiter-sent message after real review does not
Recruitee offers job board multiposting
Candidate data: four weeks after the procedure, one year with consent (AP guidance)

assumptions: Candidates in the pool gave consent to be kept for a year
unknowns: Hires per source last year
Referral bonuses paid and missed
research_questions: Which source produced hires still here after 90 days?
How many past candidates could have been re-contacted for vacancies opened last year?

tasks.short: Collect consent, call referees, request the VOG, check certificates and licences, record the outcome.

steps.what: Decide which checks apply and ask the candidate for consent and referees
Request the VOG and collect certificates and licences
Call referees with the structured questions
Check documents for consistency: dates, employers, validity

loop.input: uploaded certificate, licence or diploma image
loop.output: issuer, holder name, issue and expiry date
loop.check: name matches the candidate; expiry in the future; dates consistent with the CV timeline; mismatches are flags, never a verdict
loop.stop: one pass; unreadable documents go to the recruiter
loop.why_not_simpler: certificates come as photos in many layouts

steps.what: Record the outcome and chase missing items

tasks.design: A checklist per job profile drives consent, referee collection, the VOG request and document upload from Recruitee; reminders chase the candidate. A bounded loop reads certificates and flags expiry and mismatches. The referee call stays a call on a structured form, with no notetaker. Status shows per candidate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Checks lived in the recruiter's mail; VOG requests and certificates were chased by hand and nobody knew what was still missing.
tasks.enabler_now: Recruitee document fields, a digital VOG request flow, and models that read certificate photos under a name-and-date check.
tasks.still_hard: Referees who do not call back; the VOG applies to some roles only; the VCA register has no API I know of (model knowledge).
tasks.human_edge: Hearing in a referee's pause what the form will not say.

ambition.what: Every warehouse hire has a checked certificate before day one, not after the first incident.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter calls referees and reads flags instead of chasing paperwork; they set the check list per job profile with the HR director.

reach.learn: Wet arbeid vreemdelingen identity duties and document retention

evidence.claim: References need the candidate's consent (NVP code) and the VOG is requested through Justis
Notes and summaries become the record; keep the referee call on a form the recruiter fills
A profile built from data beyond the application is under consumer-reporting attack (Kistler v. Eightfold)

assumptions: Which roles require a VOG is decided by HR and written down
Candidates can upload documents in Recruitee
unknowns: Share of hires with a VOG requirement
Days from offer to completed checks today
research_questions: How many hires started without a completed check last year?
How many certificates on file are expired?

tasks.short: Interview candidates about work history, training and skills, with or for the hiring manager.

steps.what: Schedule the interview with candidate and manager
Prepare: reread the CV and pick questions per must-have
Hold the interview
Fill the scorecard in Recruitee
Agree the next step with the manager

tasks.design: Booking over Graph; an interview kit assembled from the profile card and a question bank per job profile (two questions per must-have, written once by people with L&D; a model may propose items for review); a structured scorecard in Recruitee. No AI notetaker and no AI interviewer: the record is the recruiter's own scorecard.
tasks.previous_blocker: Generic questions, scheduling by mail, notes in a notebook.
tasks.enabler_now: Profile cards and the question bank exist from tasks 1 and 12; Graph booking from task 4.
tasks.still_hard: Managers who improvise, and the temptation to record and summarise, which turns the summary into the record.
tasks.human_edge: The interview itself: noticing what a candidate does not say, and selling the job honestly.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in the room; around it the recruiter stops scheduling and gets a kit per candidate.

reach.learn: Structured interview design and bias in questioning

evidence.claim: Workday generated two questions per skill for 800+ skills; no evidence of better hires
Summaries become the record and store the unlawful question
Emotion inference in hiring is banned

assumptions: Managers interview on site; Teams is used for office roles
unknowns: Interviews per hire per job profile
Whether managers fill scorecards today
research_questions: How many interviews ended without a scorecard last year?

tasks.short: Check whether the must-haves, tests and sources select fairly and predict who stays; propose changes.

steps.what: Pull funnel data from Recruitee and hires and leavers from AFAS into Excel
Analyse pass-through by stage, source and site against who stayed
Review must-haves and tests against the job and the legal norms
Write the recommendation memo for the HR director and the works council

loop.input: the recruiter's bullet conclusions and the dashboard figures
loop.check: every number in the draft equals a dashboard value; claims without a bullet are flagged
loop.why_not_simpler: a template cannot phrase a conclusion

steps.what: Agree revisions with the HR director and the works council

tasks.design: A nightly join of Recruitee stages and sources with AFAS hires, probation outcomes and 90-day leavers on the data platform feeds a Power BI funnel page per site, source and job profile. The recruiter reads it, reviews the criteria, and a bounded loop drafts the memo from their conclusions. From 2027 this page is also the AI Act monitoring record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recruitee and AFAS exports were joined by hand once a year, if at all; no link to retention.
tasks.enabler_now: The nightly AFAS extract already feeds Power BI; the Recruitee API adds the funnel.
tasks.still_hard: Group-level fairness checks need data Noordhaven may not lawfully hold on candidates; small numbers per site.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing that a criterion is there because of one bad hire years ago, and arguing it away.

ambition.what: Criteria reviewed every quarter per site instead of once a year for all.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter becomes the owner of the funnel and the selection rules, with a standing item on the works council agenda.

reach.learn: The AFAS extract model and DAX measures

evidence.claim: Deployers of high-risk systems need an overseer, logs kept six months, and must inform workers' representatives (from December 2027)
The AP finds recruitment AI weak on explainability
Liability stays with the employer; the Sirius XM dismissal is not a finding of fairness
Uniper's agent found bottlenecks only with process context

assumptions: Recruitee source and stage history can be exported per candidate
Hires can be linked from Recruitee to AFAS by a key
unknowns: Which candidate attributes Noordhaven may lawfully analyse for adverse impact
90-day leavers per source last year
research_questions: Which must-have, when waived, produced hires who stayed?
What is the 90-day retention per source and site?

tasks.short: Forecast staffing needs per site and season, choose channels and budget, agree the hiring plan.

steps.what: Collect needs from site managers, the shift plan, leavers and flex use
Analyse sources, time to hire, cost per hire and seasonality
Draft the hiring plan and channel budget

loop.input: the demand view, the channel analysis and the recruiter's choices
loop.output: plan text and a budget table
loop.check: numbers trace to the dashboard; the choices are the recruiter's
loop.why_not_simpler: a plan needs prose a template cannot write

steps.what: Agree the plan with the HR director and site managers
Open vacancies, brief agencies, start campaigns

tasks.design: A demand view on the platform: headcount versus plan per site from AFAS, open vacancies from Recruitee, flex headcount from the order record, leavers in notice, and the seasonal pattern of the last two years. The funnel page from task 9 gives channel cost and speed. The plan is drafted from both; approved vacancies open in Recruitee from the plan.
tasks.previous_blocker: Demand was guessed from mails; flex headcount lived in agency CSVs.
tasks.enabler_now: The AFAS extract, the Recruitee API and the flex order record from task 11.
tasks.still_hard: Site managers who announce peaks late; agency rates negotiated outside the plan.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing that Venlo's peak starts two weeks before the forecast says.

ambition.what: A monthly demand view instead of a yearly plan, so vacancies open before the peak.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter brings the numbers to the site meeting and gains a seat in the monthly staffing decision.

reach.learn: How the FP&A model treats flex cost versus fixed headcount

evidence.claim: Workday's agent flags roles at risk of missing their fill date
Under 5% of companies using AI hiring tools saw transformational results; efficiency gains are more common

assumptions: Two years of hiring and leaver history exist in AFAS
unknowns: Seasonal flex peak per site
Channel spend per year
research_questions: How many weeks before a peak were vacancies opened last year?

tasks.short: Order flex workers from three agencies per team lead request, confirm them, and manage the agencies.

steps.what: Receive the team lead's flex request by mail or phone
Send the order to the agencies and collect their proposals
Confirm workers, check certificates and induction, tell the team lead
Weekly agency call: fill rate, no-shows, rates, disputes
Reconcile orders with agency hours and invoices for the bookkeeper

tasks.design: A flex request form (site, shift, start, weeks, skills, cost centre, approver) creates an order record; a fixed-format order mail goes to the agencies the recruiter picks; CSV replies are parsed into the order; confirmation runs the certificate and induction checklist and posts the board to the team lead in Teams. The order record is the reference the bookkeeper's invoice matcher uses. The weekly agency call stays.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders by mail and phone, three CSV layouts, and nobody knew which lines were filled.
tasks.enabler_now: Graph mail and Teams, a small CRUD app, and agencies that already send CSVs.
tasks.still_hard: Agencies that change CSV layouts; same-day requests; rates agreed by phone.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which agency sends people who show up on Monday, and telling the other two.

ambition.what: Flex workers arrive with checked certificates and a booked induction, the same as employees.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter runs an order board instead of a mailbox and gains the right to allocate orders between agencies on performance.

reach.learn: How agency invoice lines are built: rate, hours, surcharges

evidence.claim: The three agencies deliver orders, hours and invoices by mail and CSV
The hirer is responsible for flex workers' safety and must check the agency's Waadi registration

assumptions: The three agencies accept a fixed order format
Team leads will use a Teams form
unknowns: Orders per week in peak
Fill rate and no-show rate per agency
Disputed invoice lines last year
research_questions: How many order lines were unfilled at shift start last peak?
How many flex workers started without a checked certificate?

tasks.short: Write, run and evaluate applicant tests: safety quiz, forklift practical, language check, office assessments.

steps.what: Decide with L&D and the manager which test a profile needs; write items and scoring

loop.input: the job profile must-haves and the site safety manual
loop.output: candidate test items, each with the manual section it rests on
loop.check: every item cites a manual section; recruiter and L&D pick and edit
loop.stop: one draft set; nothing is used unreviewed
loop.why_not_simpler: items are free text; the bank must be written once

steps.what: Build the test as a form with rule-based scoring
Run the test with the candidate
Score and record the result
Evaluate whether the test predicts who stays and performs

tasks.design: Tests are fixed-item forms with rule-based scoring, built in Microsoft Forms or Recruitee questionnaires, booked through task 4 and scored by rule into Recruitee; the recruiter decides, the score does not. A bounded loop drafts items for L&D to review. The dashboard from task 9 links scores to retention. No AI-scored or game-based assessment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tests were Word documents scored by hand; nobody checked whether they predicted anything.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms and Recruitee questionnaires score rules for free; the retention join exists from task 9.
tasks.still_hard: Writing items that are job-related and lawful; small numbers per job profile make evaluation weak.
tasks.human_edge: Watching a candidate on the forklift course, which no quiz replaces.

ambition.what: Every test's predictive value checked each year, and dropped when it predicts nothing.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter owns the test set per job profile with L&D and can retire a test on the numbers.

reach.learn: Item writing and the VCA and forklift standards

evidence.claim: Online and game-based assessments fall under automated decision-making rules; no decision solely on the score
Evaluating candidates with AI is Annex III high-risk from December 2027
Emotion inference is banned

assumptions: Tests exist today for forklift and safety; office assessments are bought from a provider
unknowns: Tests per year per job profile
Whether any current test is scored by a model or a game
research_questions: Did test scores predict probation outcomes last year?

role.altitude: The two recruiters stop keying, chasing and scheduling and run queues: screening, flex orders, checks. They own the must-have lists, the message templates and the funnel numbers, and gain the right to refuse incomplete job orders and to choose which agency gets an order.
reach: HR Administrator: pre-boarding data from Recruitee into AFAS
Learning and Development: week-one induction and certificate booking for new hires and flex workers
Bookkeeper: the flex order record that agency invoices are matched against
HR Business Partner: 30- and 90-day check-ins with new hires and their team leads
skills_to_grow: Writing must-haves and knock-out questions that are lawful and predictive
Reading the funnel and retention dashboard and acting on it
Works council and DPIA paperwork for recruitment tools
role.ambitious_version: Every application gets a decision within one working day, every shortlisted candidate hears something every week, every flex worker arrives with a checked certificate and a booked induction, and the recruiters spend the freed hours on interviews and 30- and 90-day check-ins, which is the North Star.
